title: Correction: Understanding antibiotic decision-making for bovine respiratory disease: a survey of UK farm veterinarians
abstract: Bovine Respiratory Disease (BRD) is among the most significant economic and clinical health challenges affecting calves during the first 6 months of life, involving both the upper and lower respiratory tracts (1,2). Etiologically, BRD is a multifactorial disease arising from interactions between host susceptibility and multiple pathogens. Primary viral agents, such as bovine respiratory syncytial virus (BRSV), predispose cattle to secondary bacterial infections by Mannheimia haemolytica and Pasteurella multocida, causing severe bronchopneumonia. Accordingly, BRD control measures combine prevention, such as vaccination and herd-management strategies, with treatment, which primarily relies on antimicrobial use (3,4).Previous research reported that the disease affects 12-16% of preweaned dairy calves globally, accounting for approximately one-quarter of calf mortalities (3,5,6). Besides acute morbidity and mortality, BRD has long-term consequences into adulthood, including reduced growth rates, lower milk yield, and an increased risk of culling before the initial lactation period is completed (7,8). In addition to productivity losses, BRD is a painful condition in calves, characterised by behavioural and physiological indicators, such as reduced feed intake, prolonged lying period, and elevated inflammatory biomarkers (9,10).The economic burden is considerable, comprising direct costs, namely veterinary treatment and mortality, as well as indirect losses including reduced weight gain, prolonged time to market, and decreased reproductive performance (11). In the United Kingdom (UK), the cost per affected calf is estimated at between £30 and £80, with industry-wide impacts totalling around £50 million annually (12). These findings reinforce BRD's status as one of the most frequent causes of veterinary intervention in dairy cattle, highlighting its central role in UK livestock health management (6). The disease also accounts for a substantial proportion of antibiotic use in calves and is regarded as a priority for antimicrobial stewardship (AMS) in UK dairy farm production systems (13)(14)(15). However, there is limited knowledge about UK farm veterinarians' decision-making regarding the use of antibiotics in the treatment of BRD.Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a complex, transboundary challenge that endangers human, animal, and environmental health systems. Addressing this global issue demands a collaborative One Health approach that integrates cross-sector expertise and interventions (16)(17)(18). In this context, veterinarians' antibiotic prescribing practices intersect with broader AMR concerns, connecting farm-level decisionmaking to global health priorities. The interconnected nature of AMR, human, and animal health reflects the importance of interdisciplinary approaches that combine clinical, epidemiological, and behavioural sciences (19).While antibiotics, particularly oxytetracycline, tulathromycin, and florfenicol, remain central to BRD control, their use is increasingly scrutinised due to AMR risks (20)(21)(22). To address these concerns, the European Medicines Agency (EMA) classifies veterinary antibiotics into 4 groups (A-D) based on their public health importance to guide prudent antibiotic use. Category D ('Prudence') serves as the primary line of treatment, whereas Category B ('Restrict') is restricted to treating infections only where no alternatives are available (23). In the UK, policy frameworks such as Confronting Antimicrobial Resistance 2024 to 2029 focus on reducing unnecessary antimicrobial use through diagnostic stewardship, sensitivity testing, and evidence-based prescribing (24). However, a UK survey found that fewer than one-fifth (19%) of farm veterinarians performed antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST) when a bacterial infection was first suspected (25). Barriers to the responsible use of antibiotics include cost, time constraints, a lack of rapid diagnostic tools, and farmer expectations (25,26).International prescribing practices reveal varying approaches to BRD treatment, though macrolides and tetracyclines remain among the most commonly used antibiotic classes across regions. In the United States (US), cross-sectional surveys of veterinarians managing BRD in preweaned dairy calves showed widespread use of antibiotics as first-line treatment, most commonly tulathromycin, with florfenicol as a frequent second-line choice (9). Similarly, in Australian feedlots, national guidelines recommended tetracycline and tilmicosin as first-line agents, though severe cases may progress to tulathromycin or ceftiofur (27). Clinical trials conducted across Europe further support the efficacy of antibiotics such as tulathromycin in managing predominant bacterial infections, including M. multocida (28).In the UK context, research has focused primarily on producer practices and broad prescribing factors. Surveys of Scottish dairy farmers managing calves have reported macrolides and tetracyclines as the most commonly used antibiotics for calf pneumonia (29). Complementary insights into veterinary prescribing behaviour across the UK indicate that decisions are shaped by a combination of clinical factors (e.g., pyrexia), practical considerations (e.g., ease of administration and withdrawal periods), and external commercial pressures (e.g., supermarket contracts and assurance schemes) (30). Furthermore, ethnographic case studies highlight how AMS pressures and concerns over treatment efficacy can influence farm-level management practices, such as shifting calf housing systems to reduce disease incidence (31). However, despite the global data and UK contextual studies, none of these UK studies directly examined antibiotic usage for BRD from the specific perspective of UK farm veterinarians, leaving a significant knowledge gap regarding the factors that influence their prescribing decisions and the evidence base for BRD treatment strategies. To address this gap, the present research examines the decision-making processes and contextual factors that influence antibiotic prescribing for BRD in calves among UK farm veterinarians.The study was approved by the Research Ethics Institutional Process at Aberystwyth University (application number: 29490Ha; May 2025).The survey design was based on research by Mijares et al. (9), which investigated farm veterinarians' perspectives on treatment and diagnostic tools related to BRD in preweaned calves in the US. The survey questions were adapted for the UK context, incorporating additional questions from relevant UK-based research by Coyne et al. (25).While the original US survey drew upon either the Wisconsin or California Respiratory Scoring Systems, this modified UK survey focuses on common clinical signs (e.g., cough, dyspnoea, and nasal discharge). Also, specific antimicrobials referenced within the survey were modified -the US-specific antibiotic trade name and active ingredients being replaced with commercial products licensed and commonly used in the UK market, with classification aligned with the National Office of Animal Health (NOAH) Compendium of Animal Medicines website (32).The paper-based survey was designed using Microsoft Word (Microsoft Corporation, Redmond, WA). It was piloted with farm veterinarians (n = 27) during the Arwain DGC conference held in May 2025. Feedback gathered during this pilot study was used to assess the clarity of the phrasing, the clinical relevance of the scenarios, and the appropriate sequencing of questions. Minor amendments were required, and the survey was refined, formatted, and advanced in line with the initial feedback.The final survey comprised a total of 28 questions, including a combination of multiple-choice, textentry, Likert-scale (33), and numerical rank-order problems (1 to 3) for the first, second, and third choices of antibiotic treatment options in each scenario. Meanwhile, for the Likert-scale questions, a 5-point scale assessed importance, ranging from not at all, slightly, moderately, very, and extremely. The 3-point scale questions were adapted from the UK prior research study by Coyne et al. (25), with the following options: less likely, neutral, and more likely, never or rarely, sometimes, and often or always for the different scenarios and circumstances.The survey was divided into four main sections: demographics; clinical signs and diagnostic tools; treatment and control measures; and other factors influencing the decision to prescribe an antibiotic (see Supplementary Material). The definition of BRD for the purposes of the survey was outlined in the introduction as an infectious disease affecting the upper and lower respiratory tracts of cattle less than 6 months old.The target population for this study was UK farm veterinarians with working experience treating BRD in calves on dairy cattle farms. While there are 31,279 UK Practising Veterinary Surgeons registered with the Royal College of Veterinary Surgeons (RCVS), the relevant population for this study were the 1,760 individuals stating "farm animal" as their primary species type. The accessible sampling frame was further constrained to the 575 farm animal practitioners who had consented to their data being used for research purposes, only a proportion of whom would be expected to be treating cattle.The final valid sample size achieved (n = 95) represented approximately 16.5% of this consented population. Given the exploratory and descriptive nature of this cross-sectional study, the sample size was determined to maximise the proportion of the constrained, accessible population.The survey was disseminated in paper format during two veterinary-related events in Wales in May and July 2025. The online survey was disseminated via the official research mailing list of veterinarians who identified as UK farm-practising with the RCVS, as well as through the British and Irish Society of Animal Science (BISAS) mailing list and the newsletter of the British Cattle Veterinary Association (BCVA). It was also promoted on social media platforms. Respondent participation was voluntary and anonymous, with a reminder email and post uploaded approximately 14 days after the first broadcast messages.The survey was live for 3 months between May and August 2025; a total of 95 veterinarians responded.Data from both the paper and online surveys were recorded and extracted from Joint Information Systems Committee (JISC), and subsequently imported into Microsoft Excel (Microsoft Corporation, Redmond, WA) for initial data processing. Similarly, in Australian feedlots, national guidelines recommended tetracycline and tilmicosin as first-line agents, though severe cases may progress to tulathromycin or ceftiofur (27). Clinical trials conducted across Europe further support the efficacy of antibiotics such as tulathromycin in managing predominant bacterial infections, including M. multocida (28).In the UK context, research has focused primarily on producer practices and broad prescribing factors. Surveys of Scottish dairy farmers managing calves have reported macrolides and tetracyclines as the most commonly used antibiotics for calf pneumonia (29). Complementary insights into veterinary prescribing behaviour across the UK indicate that decisions are shaped by a combination of clinical factors (e.g., pyrexia), practical considerations (e.g., ease of administration and withdrawal periods), and external commercial pressures (e.g., supermarket contracts and assurance schemes) (30). Furthermore, ethnographic case studies highlight how AMS pressures and concerns over treatment efficacy can influence farm-level management practices, such as shifting calf housing systems to reduce disease incidence (31). However, despite the global data and UK contextual studies, none of these UK studies directly examined antibiotic usage for BRD from the specific perspective of UK farm veterinarians, leaving a significant knowledge gap regarding the factors that influence their prescribing decisions and the evidence base for BRD treatment strategies. To address this gap, the present research examines the decision-making processes and contextual factors that influence antibiotic prescribing for BRD in calves among UK farm veterinarians.The study was approved by the Research Ethics Institutional Process at Aberystwyth University (application number: 29490Ha; May 2025).The survey design was based on research by Mijares et al. (9), which investigated farm veterinarians' perspectives on treatment and diagnostic tools related to BRD in preweaned calves in the US. The survey questions were adapted for the UK context, incorporating additional questions from relevant UK-based research by Coyne et al. (25).While the original US survey drew upon either the Wisconsin or California Respiratory Scoring Systems, this modified UK survey focuses on common clinical signs (e.g., cough, dyspnoea, and nasal discharge). Also, specific antimicrobials referenced within the survey were modified -the US-specific antibiotic trade name and active ingredients being replaced with commercial products licensed and commonly used in the UK market, with classification aligned with the National Office of Animal Health (NOAH) Compendium of Animal Medicines website (32).The paper-based survey was designed using Microsoft Word (Microsoft Corporation, Redmond, WA). It was piloted with farm veterinarians (n = 27) during the Arwain DGC conference held in May 2025. Feedback gathered during this pilot study was used to assess the clarity of the phrasing, the clinical relevance of the scenarios, and the appropriate sequencing of questions. Minor amendments were required, and the survey was refined, formatted, and advanced in line with the initial feedback.The final survey comprised a total of 28 questions, including a combination of multiple-choice, textentry, Likert-scale (33), and numerical rank-order problems (1 to 3) for the first, second, and third choices of antibiotic treatment options in each scenario. Meanwhile, for the Likert-scale questions, a 5-point scale assessed importance, ranging from not at all, slightly, moderately, very, and extremely. The 3-point scale questions were adapted from the UK prior research study by Coyne et al. (25), with the following options: less likely, neutral, and more likely, never or rarely, sometimes, and often or always for the different scenarios and circumstances.The survey was divided into four main sections: demographics; clinical signs and diagnostic tools; treatment and control measures; and other factors influencing the decision to prescribe an antibiotic (see Supplementary Material). The definition of BRD for the purposes of the survey was outlined in the introduction as an infectious disease affecting the upper and lower respiratory tracts of cattle less than 6 months old.The target population for this study was UK farm veterinarians with working experience treating BRD in calves on dairy cattle farms. While there are 31,279 UK Practising Veterinary Surgeons registered with the Royal College of Veterinary Surgeons (RCVS), the relevant population for this study were the 1,760 individuals stating "farm animal" as their primary species type. The accessible sampling frame was further constrained to the 575 farm animal practitioners who had consented to their data being used for research purposes, only a proportion of whom would be expected to be treating cattle.The final valid sample size achieved (n = 95) represented approximately 16.5% of this consented population. Given the exploratory and descriptive nature of this cross-sectional study, the sample size was determined to maximise the proportion of the constrained, accessible population.The survey was disseminated in paper format during two veterinary-related events in Wales in May and July 2025. It was also promoted on social media platforms. title: Demographic and Clinical Determinants of Acute Bronchiolitis Outcomes in a Tertiary Pediatric Hospital in Dubai, United Arab Emirates
abstract: Background: Bronchiolitis is a lower respiratory tract infection that affects children under two years of age and is considered a cause of increased morbidity and healthcare costs, especially during the winter season. Despite its global burden, evidence on how local demographic or clinical factors influence outcomes in Middle Eastern populations remains limited. Objectives: This study aims to examine the descriptive epidemiology and different demographic and clinical characteristics of patients admitted with bronchiolitis, and to evaluate exploratory associations between these characteristics and various clinical outcomes, including duration of hospital admission, need for pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) admission, and need for invasive oxygen supplementation. Methods: This retrospective study included all infants aged 1-24 months who were admitted with bronchiolitis between October 1, 2022, and March 31, 2023. Electronic records from Cerner and Salama (Epic) were screened. Variables extracted included age at presentation, sex, nationality, gestational age, feeding type, family history of atopy, viral PCR results, initial oxygen saturation, and therapies received. Primary outcomes were PICU admission, maximum oxygen support, and length of stay. Associations were assessed using chi‐square or Fisher’s exact tests for categorical variables and Mann-Whitney U tests for continuous variables, with significance set at p < 0.05. Results: Of 1,804 screened encounters, 232 patients were eligible for the study. The mean (± SD) age was 6.6 ± 5.2 months, and 138 patients (59.5%) were male. Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) was detected in 101 patients (43.5%), rhinovirus/enterovirus in 29 patients (12.5%), and mixed/other viruses in 53 patients (22.8%). A high-flow nasal cannula was used in 87 cases (37.5%), but only 14 patients (6.1%) required PICU admission. None of the demographic or clinical factors showed a statistically significant effect on the chance of PICU admission or oxygen requirement. A family history of atopy was the only factor associated with a shorter length of stay (Mann-Whitney U = 2503.5; p = 0.008). Steroid therapy was more frequently administered to infants requiring greater oxygen support (chi-square = 13.971; p < 0.001), but did not shorten hospital stays or reduce PICU admissions. Conclusions: In this cohort from the United Arab Emirates, bronchiolitis outcomes were largely independent of demographic factors, viral etiology, or corticosteroid use. Adherence to international guidelines, which advocate for supportive care and discourage the routine use of glucocorticoids or bronchodilators, is likely to improve resource utilization without compromising outcomes.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Bronchiolitis imposes substantial winter-season morbidity and healthcare costs in children under two years globally, yet local determinants of outcomes in Middle Eastern populations remain insufficiently characterized. The study addresses a knowledge gap by examining how demographic and clinical factors influence acute bronchiolitis outcomes in a tertiary pediatric hospital in Dubai.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective study was conducted at a tertiary pediatric hospital in Dubai, United Arab Emirates, including infants aged 1–24 months admitted with bronchiolitis between October 1, 2022, and March 31, 2023. Electronic records from Cerner and Salama (Epic) were screened, yielding 232 eligible patients.
analysis.methods: Variables extracted included age, sex, nationality, gestational age, feeding type, family history of atopy, viral PCR results, initial oxygen saturation, and therapies received. Primary outcomes were PICU admission, maximum oxygen support, and length of stay. Associations were assessed using chi-square or Fisher’s exact tests for categorical variables and Mann-Whitney U tests for continuous variables, with significance set at p < 0.05.
analysis.main_results: Among 232 patients, the mean age was 6.6 ± 5.2 months and 59.5% were male. RSV was detected in 43.5%, rhinovirus/enterovirus in 12.5%, and mixed/other viruses in 22.8%. High-flow nasal cannula was used in 37.5%, and 6.1% required PICU admission. None of the demographic or clinical factors showed a significant effect on PICU admission or oxygen requirement, while family history of atopy was associated with a shorter length of stay (p = 0.008). Steroid therapy was more frequent in infants requiring greater oxygen support (p < 0.001) but did not reduce hospital stay or PICU admission.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that bronchiolitis outcomes in this UAE cohort were largely independent of demographic factors, viral etiology, or corticosteroid use, aligning with guideline recommendations for supportive care. The novelty lies in providing local Middle Eastern evidence on determinants of bronchiolitis outcomes, previously limited in the region.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings support adherence to international guidelines advocating supportive care and discouraging routine glucocorticoid or bronchodilator use to optimize resource utilization without compromising outcomes in pediatric bronchiolitis management.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The retrospective design and single-center setting limit generalizability, and the absence of multivariable adjustment constrains causal inference. The evidence strength is moderate due to these limitations and the exploratory nature of associations.

analysis.summary_en: This retrospective study from a tertiary pediatric hospital in Dubai examined determinants of acute bronchiolitis outcomes among 232 infants aged 1–24 months admitted between October 2022 and March 2023. The study found that demographic factors, viral etiology, and corticosteroid use did not significantly influence PICU admission or oxygen requirements, while a family history of atopy was associated with shorter hospital stays. RSV was the most detected virus, and steroid therapy was more common in infants with greater oxygen needs but did not improve outcomes. The authors conclude that outcomes were largely independent of these factors, supporting adherence to supportive care guidelines to optimize resource use. The single-center, retrospective design and lack of multivariable adjustment limit generalizability and causal inference, warranting moderate confidence in the findings.

title_zh: 阿拉伯联合酋长国迪拜一家三级儿科医院急性细支气管炎结果的人口统计学和临床​​决定因素
source_body_en: Background: Bronchiolitis is a lower respiratory tract infection that affects children under two years of age and is considered a cause of increased morbidity and healthcare costs, especially during the winter season. Despite its global burden, evidence on how local demographic or clinical factors influence outcomes in Middle Eastern populations remains limited. Objectives: This study aims to examine the descriptive epidemiology and different demographic and clinical characteristics of patients admitted with bronchiolitis, and to evaluate exploratory associations between these characteristics and various clinical outcomes, including duration of hospital admission, need for pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) admission, and need for invasive oxygen supplementation. Methods: This retrospective study included all infants aged 1-24 months who were admitted with bronchiolitis between October 1, 2022, and March 31, 2023. Electronic records from Cerner and Salama (Epic) were screened. Variables extracted included age at presentation, sex, nationality, gestational age, feeding type, family history of atopy, viral PCR results, initial oxygen saturation, and therapies received. Primary outcomes were PICU admission, maximum oxygen support, and length of stay. Associations were assessed using chi‐square or Fisher’s exact tests for categorical variables and Mann-Whitney U tests for continuous variables, with significance set at p < 0.05. Results: Of 1,804 screened encounters, 232 patients were eligible for the study. The mean (± SD) age was 6.6 ± 5.2 months, and 138 patients (59.5%) were male. Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) was detected in 101 patients (43.5%), rhinovirus/enterovirus in 29 patients (12.5%), and mixed/other viruses in 53 patients (22.8%). A high-flow nasal cannula was used in 87 cases (37.5%), but only 14 patients (6.1%) required PICU admission. None of the demographic or clinical factors showed a statistically significant effect on the chance of PICU admission or oxygen requirement. A family history of atopy was the only factor associated with a shorter length of stay (Mann-Whitney U = 2503.5; p = 0.008). Steroid therapy was more frequently administered to infants requiring greater oxygen support (chi-square = 13.971; p < 0.001), but did not shorten hospital stays or reduce PICU admissions. Conclusions: In this cohort from the United Arab Emirates, bronchiolitis outcomes were largely independent of demographic factors, viral etiology, or corticosteroid use. Adherence to international guidelines, which advocate for supportive care and discourage the routine use of glucocorticoids or bronchodilators, is likely to improve resource utilization without compromising outcomes.
abstract_zh: 背景:细支气管炎是一种影响两岁以下儿童的下呼吸道感染,被认为是发病率和医疗费用增加的原因,特别是在冬季。尽管存在全球负担,但有关当地人口或临床因素如何影响中东人群结果的证据仍然有限。目的:本研究旨在检查毛细支气管炎患者的描述性流行病学以及不同的人口统计学和临床​​特征,并评估这些特征与各种临床结果之间的探索性关联,包括住院时间、入院儿科重症监护病房(PICU)的需要以及有创供氧的需要。方法:这项回顾性研究纳入了 2022 年 10 月 1 日至 2023 年 3 月 31 日期间因细支气管炎入院的所有 1-24 个月婴儿。对 Cerner 和 Salama (Epic) 的电子记录进行了筛选。提取的变量包括就诊年龄、性别、国籍、胎龄、喂养类型、过敏家族史、病毒 PCR 结果、初始氧饱和度和接受的治疗。主要结局是 PICU 入住、最大氧气支持和住院时间。使用卡方或 Fisher 精确检验对分类变量以及 Mann-Whitney U 检验对连续变量进行评估,显着性设置为 p < 0.05。结果:在 1,804 例筛查病例中,232 名患者符合研究资格。平均 (± SD) 年龄为 6.6 ± 5.2 个月,138 名患者 (59.5%) 为男性。101 名患者(43.5%)检测到呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV),29 名患者(12.5%)检测到鼻病毒/肠道病毒,53 名患者(22.8%)检测到混合/其他病毒。87例(37.5%)使用高流量鼻导管,但只有14例(6.1%)需要入住PICU。人口统计学或临床因素均未显示出对 PICU 入住机会或氧气需求有统计学上的显着影响。特应性家族史是与较短住院时间相关的唯一因素(Mann-Whitney U = 2503.5;p = 0.008)。类固醇治疗更频繁地用于需要更多氧气支持的婴儿(卡方 = 13.971;p < 0.001),但并没有缩短住院时间或减少 PICU 入院率。结论:在来自阿拉伯联合酋长国的队列中,细支气管炎的结果在很大程度上与人口因素、病毒病因或皮质类固醇的使用无关。遵守提倡支持性护理并阻止常规使用糖皮质激素或支气管扩张剂的国际指南可能会在不影响结果的情况下提高资源利用率。

title: Disparities in Nirsevimab Uptake Over 2 Seasons
abstract: Nirsevimab, a monoclonal antibody for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) prophylaxis, debuted during the 2023 to 2024 RSV season. Despite universal recommendation, both incomplete uptake and disparities in nirsevimab receipt exist.1,2 Nirsevimab administration is important because it is highly effective in preventing RSV infection and hospitalization in young infants.3 The objective of this study was to determine if (1) nirsevimab uptake increased within a large pediatric primary care network and (2) if previously identified disparities persisted in its second RSV season.A cohort of infants younger than 8 months from 32 primary care practices across New Jersey and Pennsylvania within the Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia network was generated as previously described.1 Infants with maternal RSV vaccination were excluded. The 2023 to 2024 RSV season was defined as October 1, 2023, through March 31, 2024, and the 2024 to 2025 RSV season as October 1, 2024, through March 31, 2025. We included infants ineligible to receive nirsevimab in the birth hospital due to being born outside of RSV season (April through September) and, therefore, reliant on their primary care practice to receive it, allowing the exploration of factors potentially associated with nirsevimab uptake within the context of the patient’s medical home.Nirsevimab administration and patient age, sex, race and ethnicity, birthweight, insurance status, Childhood Opportunity Index (COI), and visit type were extracted from the electronic health record (EHR).4,5 Race and ethnicity data were self-reported by patients in the EHR. Although race is a social construct, it is included in the analyses because differences in nirsevimab receipt can highlight potential inequities. Vaccine adherence analyses (up to date for Haemophilus influenzae type b, poliovirus, Streptococcus pneumoniae, diphtheria, tetanus, and pertussis by age 9 months) were conducted as previously described.1Descriptive comparisons of uptake across subgroups are presented as unadjusted proportions. Logistic regression was used to determine factors associated with nirsevimab receipt during each season. We fit a pooled logistic regression model including covariates and season-by-covariate interaction terms. Adjusted ORs and 95% CIs were estimated, and interaction terms were used. Inverse probability weighting was used to address missing data.The eligible primary care cohort included 13 897 patients across both seasons (Supplement Figure 1). Comparable with the 2023 to 2024 season, patients in the 2024 to 2025 season were majority male (51.7%), White (53.0%), non-Hispanic/Latino (81.7%), and nonpublicly insured (64.8%) (Table 1). Preterm birth was not included in Figure 1 as prematurity was colinear with low birthweight as described in our previous work. Although nirsevimab uptake increased from 35% in the 2023 to 2024 season to 67% in the 2024 to 2025 season, lower rates of nirsevimab administration to infants with public insurance (OR, 0.58; 95% CI, 0.50–0.67 compared with private insurance), of Black race (OR, 0.67; 95% CI, 0.56–0.82 compared with White infants), and at an older age at start of RSV season (OR, 0.81; 95% CI, 0.79–0.84 for each additional month) persisted into season 2 (Figure 1). Lower COI no longer remained significant (OR, 0.90; 95% CI 0.71–1.14).Overall, 23.5% of children received nirsevimab at nurse (vaccine administration only) visits. Notably, infants of White race (30.9%), with very high COI (32.9%), and with nonpublic insurance (31.1%) had higher unadjusted rates of nirsevimab administration at nurse visits compared with those of Black race (7.1%), with public insurance (8.4%), and with low COI (6.4%). Infants who were fully vaccinated (38.7%–75.5%), partially vaccinated (21.7%–43.3%), and unvaccinated (0.7%–2.4%) against other routine pathogens all increased nirsevimab uptake from the 2023–2024 to 2024–2025 RSV season.Although primary care nirsevimab uptake doubled between the 2023–2024 and 2024–2025 RSV season, the majority of previously identified disparities in RSV administration remained across this large, diverse primary care network. These data suggest that targeted interventions are required to increase protection for all infants at risk of RSV infection.Infants who were publicly insured or Black remained significantly less likely to receive nirsevimab. The reasons for the observed disparities are unclear. Stark differences in rates of nirsevimab administration at nurse visits—encounters scheduled outside of normal well and sick visits and specifically created for vaccine administration—suggest health care access might contribute. Future work could explore interventions to increase nirsevimab uptake by expanding access to nurse visits and encouraging uptake during sick visits for infants with mild illnesses. Additional factors including institutional racism and differences in trust in vaccine safety among sociodemographic strata may also contribute but were not explored in the current study.Unsurprisingly, nirsevimab uptake was highest among those fully vaccinated with routine immunizations, which has been shown with other respiratory vaccines.6 Although all groups increased uptake from the 2023–2024 season to the 2024–2025 season, universally unvaccinated children almost never received nirsevimab.Limitations include the single-center study design, which limits generalizability, and inability to identify reasons for lack of nirsevimab administration, which would help guide quality improvement efforts. Although other studies confirm these disparities, to our knowledge, this is the first to demonstrate that disparities persist across multiple seasons despite increased uptake and demands examination of the drivers of these disparities to inform efforts to increase nirsevimab administration for all eligible infants.7–9

Notably, infants of White race (30.9%), with very high COI (32.9%), and with nonpublic insurance (31.1%) had higher unadjusted rates of nirsevimab administration at nurse visits compared with those of Black race (7.1%), with public insurance (8.4%), and with low COI (6.4%). Infants who were fully vaccinated (38.7%–75.5%), partially vaccinated (21.7%–43.3%), and unvaccinated (0.7%–2.4%) against other routine pathogens all increased nirsevimab uptake from the 2023–2024 to 2024–2025 RSV season.Although primary care nirsevimab uptake doubled between the 2023–2024 and 2024–2025 RSV season, the majority of previously identified disparities in RSV administration remained across this large, diverse primary care network. These data suggest that targeted interventions are required to increase protection for all infants at risk of RSV infection.Infants who were publicly insured or Black remained significantly less likely to receive nirsevimab. The reasons for the observed disparities are unclear. Stark differences in rates of nirsevimab administration at nurse visits—encounters scheduled outside of normal well and sick visits and specifically created for vaccine administration—suggest health care access might contribute. Future work could explore interventions to increase nirsevimab uptake by expanding access to nurse visits and encouraging uptake during sick visits for infants with mild illnesses. Additional factors including institutional racism and differences in trust in vaccine safety among sociodemographic strata may also contribute but were not explored in the current study.Unsurprisingly, nirsevimab uptake was highest among those fully vaccinated with routine immunizations, which has been shown with other respiratory vaccines.6 Although all groups increased uptake from the 2023–2024 season to the 2024–2025 season, universally unvaccinated children almost never received nirsevimab.Limitations include the single-center study design, which limits generalizability, and inability to identify reasons for lack of nirsevimab administration, which would help guide quality improvement efforts. Although other studies confirm these disparities, to our knowledge, this is the first to demonstrate that disparities persist across multiple seasons despite increased uptake and demands examination of the drivers of these disparities to inform efforts to increase nirsevimab administration for all eligible infants.7–9

title: Quality Improvement Initiative to Reduce Inappropriate Viral Testing within the Pediatric Emergency Department.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: The American Academy of Pediatrics Section on Emergency Medicine's Choosing Wisely Campaign includes recommendations discouraging comprehensive viral panel testing in children with suspected respiratory viral illness. In the year preceding project implementation, our free-standing pediatric emergency department (PED) ordered comprehensive respiratory pathogen panels (RPPs) in 11.9% of all visits, and 50% of those lacked a clinical indication. This project aimed to reduce the percentage of PED visits with RPP orders from 11.9% to 9% over a 6-month viral respiratory season. METHODS: We conducted four major interventions over 2 plan-do-study-act cycles. Interventions included developing a clinical guideline for viral testing, performing provider education, introducing a narrower-spectrum Quad (influenza A/B, COVID-19, and respiratory syncytial virus) polymerase chain reaction (PCR) test, and adding an order-entry indication requirement for RPPs, which also served as a just-in-time educational tool for providers. We tracked data via a clinical dashboard and through periodic chart reviews. RESULTS: Of the 43,283 patient visits during the project period, the percentage of PED RPP orders decreased from 11.9% at baseline to 6.8% during the intervention period and remained at 6.8% in the following respiratory season. The project had sustained cost savings of over $300,000 in RPP testing each year. The decrease in RPP orders did not lead to an increase in the cumulative use of other viral tests. CONCLUSIONS: This quality improvement initiative significantly improved and sustained comprehensive viral PCR testing practices in the PED without increasing the use of alternative respiratory viral testing.

abstract_zh: 简介:美国儿科学会急诊医学科的明智选择运动提出了不鼓励对疑似呼吸道病毒性疾病儿童进行全面病毒检测的建议。在项目实施的前一年,我们的独立儿科急诊科 (PED) 在 11.9% 的就诊中订购了综合呼吸道病原体检测 (RPP),其中 50% 缺乏临床指征。该项目旨在在 6 个月的病毒性呼吸道疾病季节中,将 RPP 订单下 PED 就诊的比例从 11.9% 减少到 9%。方法:我们在 2 个计划-实施-研究-行动周期中进行了四次主要干预措施。干预措施包括制定病毒检测临床指南、开展提供者教育、引入窄谱 Quad(A/B 型流感、COVID-19 和呼吸道合胞病毒)聚合酶链反应 (PCR) 测试,以及增加 RPP 的订单输入指示要求,这也可作为提供者的即时教育工具。我们通过临床仪表板和定期图表审查来跟踪数据。结果:在项目期间的 43,283 名患者就诊中,PED RPP 命令的百分比从基线的 11.9% 下降到干预期间的 6.8%,并在接下来的呼吸季节保持在 6.8%。该项目每年在 RPP 测试中节省了超过 300,000 美元的成本。RPP订单的减少并没有导致其他病毒检测累计使用量的增加。结论:这项质量改进举措显着改善并维持了 PED 中全面的病毒 PCR 检测实践,而无需增加替代呼吸道病毒检测的使用。

title: Characterisation of respiratory viral infections in hospitalised adults
abstract: Respiratory viral infections (RVIs) are major causes of adult hospitalisation, but their clinical course is heterogeneous and only partly explained by viral aetiology. Previous studies have often examined individual pathogens, particularly influenza, severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), limiting understanding of shared clinical patterns across adult hospitalised RVI. This thesis investigated clinical and biological heterogeneity in adults hospitalised with acute respiratory illness (ARI) and polymerase chain reaction (PCR)-confirmed RVI. It used the Understanding Infection, Viral Exacerbation and Respiratory Symptoms at Admission-Longitudinal (UNIVERSAL) study, a prospective multicentre United Kingdom (UK) observational cohort of adults hospitalised with a broad range of RVIs, a pooled multicentre RSV cohort and a nested interleukin-33/serum stimulation 2 (IL-33/ST2) biomarker subcohort. Symptom composition differed across viral groups, particularly for fever-related and nasal symptom domains, whereas lower respiratory and systemic symptoms were near universal across virus groups. Strict World Health Organization severe acute respiratory infection (WHO SARI) criteria captured only part of the adult hospitalised RVI spectrum, with lower capture for SARS-CoV-2 and rhino/enterovirus (RhV/EV) than for influenza and RSV. Non-capture was driven mainly by absence of fever symptoms and symptom duration beyond 10 days. Latent class analysis identified three host-derived phenotypes: an asthma-eosinophilic phenotype with shorter pre-admission symptom duration, a multimorbid cardiorenal-inflammatory phenotype, and a chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) associated phenotype with prolonged pre-admission respiratory and systemic symptoms. These phenotypes cut across viral groups and were associated with severe disease, particularly sustained respiratory failure. In adults hospitalised with RSV, age-based thresholds aligned with current UK RSV vaccine eligibility showed limited post-admission prognostic discrimination. A model incorporating age, COPD, active or previous cancer and dementia provided more informative internally validated risk stratification, suggesting that poor-outcome risk is only partially captured by chronological age alone. In the biomarker subcohort, serum soluble ST2 (sST2) and the nasal oxidised:reduced IL-33 ratio were independently associated with severe disease after adjustment for viral group, suggesting complementary systemic and upper-airway host-response signals. Overall, this thesis shows that pathogen identity, WHO SARI classification and age thresholds provide clinically useful but incomplete perspectives on hospitalised adult RVI. By integrating symptom presentation, symptom duration, host phenotype, RSV post-admission risk and IL-33/ST2 biology, it provides a framework for broader hospital ARI surveillance, outcome stratification, and future biomarker-informed research.

source_records.title: Characterisation of respiratory viral infections in hospitalised adults
source_records.abstract: Respiratory viral infections (RVIs) are major causes of adult hospitalisation, but their clinical course is heterogeneous and only partly explained by viral aetiology. Previous studies have often examined individual pathogens, particularly influenza, severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), limiting understanding of shared clinical patterns across adult hospitalised RVI. This thesis investigated clinical and biological heterogeneity in adults hospitalised with acute respiratory illness (ARI) and polymerase chain reaction (PCR)-confirmed RVI. It used the Understanding Infection, Viral Exacerbation and Respiratory Symptoms at Admission-Longitudinal (UNIVERSAL) study, a prospective multicentre United Kingdom (UK) observational cohort of adults hospitalised with a broad range of RVIs, a pooled multicentre RSV cohort and a nested interleukin-33/serum stimulation 2 (IL-33/ST2) biomarker subcohort. Symptom composition differed across viral groups, particularly for fever-related and nasal symptom domains, whereas lower respiratory and systemic symptoms were near universal across virus groups. Strict World Health Organization severe acute respiratory infection (WHO SARI) criteria captured only part of the adult hospitalised RVI spectrum, with lower capture for SARS-CoV-2 and rhino/enterovirus (RhV/EV) than for influenza and RSV. Non-capture was driven mainly by absence of fever symptoms and symptom duration beyond 10 days. Latent class analysis identified three host-derived phenotypes: an asthma-eosinophilic phenotype with shorter pre-admission symptom duration, a multimorbid cardiorenal-inflammatory phenotype, and a chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) associated phenotype with prolonged pre-admission respiratory and systemic symptoms. These phenotypes cut across viral groups and were associated with severe disease, particularly sustained respiratory failure. In adults hospitalised with RSV, age-based thresholds aligned with current UK RSV vaccine eligibility showed limited post-admission prognostic discrimination. A model incorporating age, COPD, active or previous cancer and dementia provided more informative internally validated risk stratification, suggesting that poor-outcome risk is only partially captured by chronological age alone. In the biomarker subcohort, serum soluble ST2 (sST2) and the nasal oxidised:reduced IL-33 ratio were independently associated with severe disease after adjustment for viral group, suggesting complementary systemic and upper-airway host-response signals. Overall, this thesis shows that pathogen identity, WHO SARI classification and age thresholds provide clinically useful but incomplete perspectives on hospitalised adult RVI. By integrating symptom presentation, symptom duration, host phenotype, RSV post-admission risk and IL-33/ST2 biology, it provides a framework for broader hospital ARI surveillance, outcome stratification, and future biomarker-informed research.

abstract_zh: 呼吸道病毒感染(RVI)是成人住院的主要原因,但其临床病程各不相同,并且只能部分由病毒病因学解释。先前的研究经常检查个体病原体,特别是流感、严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒 2 (SARS-CoV-2) 和呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV),限制了对成人住院 RVI 共同临床模式的了解。本论文研究了因急性呼吸道疾病 (ARI) 住院的成人患者的临床和生物学异质性以及经聚合酶链反应 (PCR) 确诊的 RVI。它使用了入院时了解感染、病毒恶化和呼吸道症状纵向 (UNIVERSAL) 研究、一项前瞻性多中心英国 (UK) 因各种 RVI 住院成人观察队列、一个汇总的多中心 RSV 队列和一个巢式白细胞介素 33/血清刺激 2 (IL-33/ST2) 生物标志物子队列。不同病毒组的症状构成不同,特别是与发烧相关和鼻部症状领域,而下呼吸道和全身症状在不同病毒组中几乎普遍存在。严格的世界卫生组织严重急性呼吸道感染 (WHO SARI) 标准仅涵盖了成人住院 RVI 谱系的一部分,其中 SARS-CoV-2 和犀牛/肠道病毒 (RhV/EV) 的捕获率低于流感和 RSV。未捕获的主要原因是没有发烧症状且症状持续时间超过 10 天。潜类别分析确定了三种源自宿主的表型:入院前症状持续时间较短的哮喘嗜酸性粒细胞表型、多病性心肾炎症表型以及入院前呼吸和全身症状延长的慢性阻塞性肺病(COPD)相关表型。这些表型跨越病毒组,并与严重疾病相关,特别是持续性呼吸衰竭。在因 RSV 住院的成人中,与当前英国 RSV 疫苗资格一致的基于年龄的阈值显示入院后预后歧视有限。纳入年龄、慢性阻塞性肺病、活动性或既往癌症和痴呆症的模型提供了更多信息,内部验证的风险分层,表明仅按实际年龄仅部分捕获不良结果风险。在生物标志物亚组中,血清可溶性 ST2 (sST2) 和鼻氧化:还原性 IL-33 比率在调整病毒组后与严重疾病独立相关,表明全身和上呼吸道宿主反应信号是互补的。总体而言,本文表明病原体身份、WHO SARI 分类和年龄阈值为住院成人 RVI 提供了临床上有用但不完整的观点。通过整合症状表现、症状持续时间、宿主表型、RSV 入院后风险和 IL-33/ST2 生物学,它为更广泛的医院 ARI 监测、结果分层和未来的生物标志物研究提供了一个框架。

title: Mechanism and spectrum of inhibition of viral polymerases by 2′-deoxy-2′-β-fluoro-4′-azidocytidine or azvudine
abstract: The therapeutic value of antiviral nucleoside analogs was highlighted during the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic, with remdesivir and molnupiravir repurposed for their broad-spectrum antiviral activity. The cytidine analog azvudine (FNC) has recently gained attention as a potential treatment for human immunodeficiency virus type 1 (HIV-1) and severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection. Considering the distinct substrate specificities of HIV-1 reverse transcriptase (RT) and SARS-CoV-2 RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp), a unifying mechanism of inhibition remains elusive. Here, we assessed the inhibitory effects of FNC’s active triphosphate form, FNC-TP, across several viral polymerases. The relative efficiency of FNC-TP incorporation followed the order: HIV-1 RT > hepatitis C virus (HCV) RdRp > respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) RdRp > dengue virus type 2 (DENV-2) RdRp ≫ SARS-CoV-2 RdRp. Its incorporation caused chain-termination in all polymerases tested. Antiviral activity against HIV-1 has previously been demonstrated and is here shown with DENV-2. Collectively, the data show that inhibition of viral polymerases by FNC-TP can translate to antiviral activity against both retroviruses and RNA viruses, but the link is not evident for SARS-CoV-2. FNC-TP is a poor substrate for SARS-CoV-2 RdRp, and FNC lacks significant antiviral activity against SARS-CoV-2 in cell culture.

title_zh: 2′-脱氧-2′-β-氟-4′-叠氮胞苷或阿兹夫定抑制病毒聚合酶的机制和谱
source_body_en: The therapeutic value of antiviral nucleoside analogs was highlighted during the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic, with remdesivir and molnupiravir repurposed for their broad-spectrum antiviral activity. The cytidine analog azvudine (FNC) has recently gained attention as a potential treatment for human immunodeficiency virus type 1 (HIV-1) and severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection. Considering the distinct substrate specificities of HIV-1 reverse transcriptase (RT) and SARS-CoV-2 RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp), a unifying mechanism of inhibition remains elusive. Here, we assessed the inhibitory effects of FNC’s active triphosphate form, FNC-TP, across several viral polymerases. The relative efficiency of FNC-TP incorporation followed the order: HIV-1 RT > hepatitis C virus (HCV) RdRp > respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) RdRp > dengue virus type 2 (DENV-2) RdRp ≫ SARS-CoV-2 RdRp. Its incorporation caused chain-termination in all polymerases tested. Antiviral activity against HIV-1 has previously been demonstrated and is here shown with DENV-2. Collectively, the data show that inhibition of viral polymerases by FNC-TP can translate to antiviral activity against both retroviruses and RNA viruses, but the link is not evident for SARS-CoV-2. FNC-TP is a poor substrate for SARS-CoV-2 RdRp, and FNC lacks significant antiviral activity against SARS-CoV-2 in cell culture.
abstract_zh: 抗病毒核苷类似物的治疗价值在 2019 年冠状病毒病 (COVID-19) 大流行期间得到强调,瑞德西韦和莫努匹拉韦因其广谱抗病毒活性而被重新利用。胞苷类似物阿兹夫定 (FNC) 最近作为治疗人类免疫缺陷病毒 1 型 (HIV-1) 和严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒 2 (SARS-CoV-2) 感染的潜在疗法而受到关注。考虑到 HIV-1 逆转录酶 (RT) 和 SARS-CoV-2 RNA 依赖性 RNA 聚合酶 (RdRp) 不同的底物特异性,统一的抑制机制仍然难以捉摸。在这里,我们评估了 FNC 的活性三磷酸盐形式 FNC-TP 对几种病毒聚合酶的抑制作用。FNC-TP掺入的相对效率遵循以下顺序:HIV-1 RT>丙型肝炎病毒(HCV)RdRp>呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)RdRp>登革热病毒2型(DENV-2)RdRp≫SARS-CoV-2 RdRp。它的掺入导致所有测试的聚合酶链终止。针对 HIV-1 的抗病毒活性先前已得到证实,此处显示了 DENV-2 的抗病毒活性。总的来说,数据表明,FNC-TP 对病毒聚合酶的抑制可以转化为针对逆转录病毒和 RNA 病毒的抗病毒活性,但对于 SARS-CoV-2,这种联系并不明显。FNC-TP 是 SARS-CoV-2 RdRp 的较差底物,并且 FNC 在细胞培养物中缺乏针对 SARS-CoV-2 的显着抗病毒活性。

title: Biomarkers and Risk Factors Associated with Apnea in Hospitalized Infants with Acute Respiratory Infection
abstract: Apnea is a potentially life-threatening complication of severe acute respiratory infection (SARI) in early infancy; however, its determinants remain incompletely understood. Between 2011 and 2013, we conducted a population-based, cross-sectional, multicenter study in Buenos Aires, Argentina. We examined epidemiological, clinical, virological, and immunological factors associated with apnea in a population-based cohort of 2376 infants younger than five months hospitalized due to SARI. Using hierarchical multivariable logistic regression, we identified preterm birth, cesarean section, previous NICU admission, age under two months, and severe household crowding as independent predictors of apnea. RSV infection was inversely associated with apnea, and IL-5 levels in respiratory secretions were significantly lower among infants with apnea, suggesting a qualitatively different immune response in this group. Taken together, these findings indicate that apnea during SARI in early infancy is primarily driven by biological immaturity and adverse environmental conditions.
authors: on behalf of The INFANT Respiratory Network

source_body_en: Apnea is a potentially life-threatening complication of severe acute respiratory infection (SARI) in early infancy; however, its determinants remain incompletely understood. Between 2011 and 2013, we conducted a population-based, cross-sectional, multicenter study in Buenos Aires, Argentina. We examined epidemiological, clinical, virological, and immunological factors associated with apnea in a population-based cohort of 2376 infants younger than five months hospitalized due to SARI. Using hierarchical multivariable logistic regression, we identified preterm birth, cesarean section, previous NICU admission, age under two months, and severe household crowding as independent predictors of apnea. RSV infection was inversely associated with apnea, and IL-5 levels in respiratory secretions were significantly lower among infants with apnea, suggesting a qualitatively different immune response in this group. Taken together, these findings indicate that apnea during SARI in early infancy is primarily driven by biological immaturity and adverse environmental conditions.
abstract_zh: 呼吸暂停是婴儿早期严重急性呼吸道感染 (SARI) 的一种可能危及生命的并发症;然而,其决定因素仍不完全清楚。2011 年至 2013 年间,我们在阿根廷布宜诺斯艾利斯进行了一项基于人群的横断面多中心研究。我们在一个由 2376 名因 SARI 住院的 5 个月以下婴儿组成的人群队列中检查了与呼吸暂停相关的流行病学、临床、病毒学和免疫学因素。使用分层多变量逻辑回归,我们确定早产、剖腹产、既往 NICU 入住、年龄不到两个月和严重的家庭拥挤是呼吸暂停的独立预测因素。RSV 感染与呼吸暂停呈负相关,患有呼吸暂停的婴儿呼吸道分泌物中的 IL-5 水平显着较低,表明该组婴儿的免疫反应存在质的不同。总而言之,这些发现表明婴儿早期 SARI 期间的呼吸暂停主要是由生物不成熟和不利的环境条件引起的。

title: Impacts of conventional and high-oleic soybean oil supplementation on rumen microbiology, physiology, immunity, and growth of recently weaned Brangus steers
abstract: Lay Summary High-oleic soybean oil (HOSBO) has a different fatty acid (FA) profile than conventional soybean oil (CSBO), which may lead to distinct effects on rumen microbiology, immune function, and growth when included in the diet of steers. Thus, the current experiment evaluated the effects of HOSBO, CSBO, and no oil supplementation on rumen microbiology, physiology, immunity, and growth of Brangus steers maintained in a forage-based system during the preconditioning phase. Although HOSBO and CSBO supplementation had minimal effects on rumen microbiology, it altered circulating FA profiles. The CSBO increased serum linoleic acid, whereas the HOSBO increased oleic acid. These differences in circulating FA were associated with distinct vaccine responses: steers receiving CSBO had stronger antibody responses to bovine viral diarrhea virus (BVDV), whereas those receiving HOSBO mounted stronger responses to bovine respiratory syncytial virus (BRSV). Growth also differed, with HOSBO-supplemented steers tending to be heavier than steers receiving CSBO by the end of the experiment. Overall, CSBO or HOSBO had minimal effects on rumen microbiology, but CSBO enhanced the immune response to BVDV, HOSBO enhanced the response to BRSV, and HOSBO promoted greater growth than CSBO.

abstract_zh: 总结 高油酸大豆油 (HOSBO) 的脂肪酸 (FA) 特征与传统大豆油 (CSBO) 不同,当添加到阉牛日粮中时,可能会对瘤胃微生物、免疫功能和生长产生明显影响。因此,本实验评估了 HOSBO、CSBO 和无油补充对在预处理阶段维持在基于饲料的系统中的布兰格斯公牛的瘤胃微生物、生理、免疫和生长的影响。尽管补充 HOSBO 和 CSBO 对瘤胃微生物影响极小,但它改变了循环 FA 谱。CSBO 增加血清亚油酸,而 HOSBO 增加油酸。循环FA的这些差异与不同的疫苗反应相关:接受CSBO的公牛对牛病毒性腹泻病毒(BVDV)有更强的抗体反应,而接受HOSBO的公牛对牛呼吸道合胞病毒(BRSV)有更强的反应。生长也不同,在实验结束时补充 HOSBO 的阉牛往往比接受 CSBO 的阉牛更重。总体而言,CSBO或HOSBO对瘤胃微生物学的影响很小,但CSBO增强了对BVDV的免疫反应,HOSBO增强了对BRSV的反应,并且HOSBO比CSBO促进了更大的生长。

title: КЛІНІКО-ПАТОГЕНЕТИЧНІ ТЕНДЕНЦІЇ ПНЕВМОНІЙ У ДІТЕЙ НА СУЧАСНОМУ ЕТАПІ
abstract: Pneumonia is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in children under 5 years of age worldwide. Although most pneumonia-related deaths in children occur in developing countries, the burden of the disease is significant and there are significant health care costs associated with pneumonia in developed countries. The number of pneumonia deaths worldwide was estimated to be 0.76 million, while the all-cause mortality rate was 5.5 per 1000 live births in 2015. Although pneumonia incidence and mortality rates have declined significantly, hospital admissions and hospitalizations are increasing in both developing and developed countries. In recent large epidemiological studies in the United States (US), the annual incidence of communityacquired pneumonia (CAP) requiring hospitalization was 15.7 cases per 10,000 children, with the highest rate among children under 2 years of age, and similar trends are observed in Asian countries. As a result of these comprehensive etiological examinations in children, pathogens were identified in 81% of cases, viruses in 73%, pyogenic bacteria in 7%, and atypical bacteria such as M. The most frequently identified viruses were respiratory syncytial virus and parainfluenza virus, although adenovirus and human rhinovirus were the second most frequently identified viruses in a specific cohort of these studies. Given such a wide variety of etiological factors with the predominance of viral agents, especially in children under 5 years of age, it is possible to consider the presence of a type-specific clinical picture - pneumonic status with a layering of obstructive and catarrhal manifestations that are so characteristic of children of early and younger age. Objective: To establish clinical and pathogenetic relationships in the course of pneumonia in young children. Materials and methods. The medical histories of 36 children under 5 years of age who were being treated in the pulmonary monological department of the Uzhhorod City Clinical Children’s Hospital were processed. Children were admitted to the department for treatment on the 3rd - 5th day of the disease. The average age of the patients was 3.8±0.7 years. The examined group of children consisted of 19 boys and 17 girls. Clinical parameters (palpation, percussion, auscultation data) and paraclinical data - radiographic changes detected in pneumonia in children were recorded. Data were analyzed for statistical significance and search for their relationships (using SPPS21 (IBM Statistics.New York. USA)), descriptive statistics, Pearson Chi-Square analysis, relative risk (risk ratio) were used. Low-productive cough was observed in 92% of cases and bothered patients throughout the day. Dyspnea was not observed in 5 (14%) children, and in 17 (47%) cases, expiratory dyspnea was noted, mixed in 14 (39%). Manifestations of catarrhal syndrome - difficulty in nasal breathing, mucous discharge were observed in 25 (69%) patients. By localization of pneumonia, lower-lobe pneumonia was mainly found in 27 (75%) cases, upper-lobe pneumonia in 7 (19%) children and combined upper-lobe and lower-lobe pneumonia in 2 (6%) patients. The results of physical methods of research revealed that percussion dullness of percussion sound was observed in 18 (50%) cases, tympanitis in 15 (42%) patients, auscultatively children with manifestations of hard breathing prevailed in 32 (88.9%), locally weakened vesicular was heard in 14 (38.9%) cases. Auscultatively dry rales of various caliber were heard in 27 (75%) children, wet rales - in 9 (25%) patients, the phenomenon of crepitation was heard only in 21 (58.3%) cases. The X-ray picture of pneumonia in children was confirmed by the presence of foci of shadowing in all children and was accompanied in 21 (58.3) patients by an increase in the bronchopulmonary pattern on the X-ray. Analysis of clinical and paraclinical indicators revealed a high degree of reliable relationships between the pulmonary picture on the X-ray and difficult nasal breathing (p = 0.009), between the localization of the focus of pneumonia in the lower lobes of the lungs and the presence of hard breathing (p = 0.008). A somewhat lower degree of reliability was observed between the pulmonary picture on the X-ray and the phenomena of shortness of breath (p = 0.022) and between difficult nasal breathing and crepitus (p = 0.030). The revealed patterns indicate a close pathogenetic relationship between the upper and lower parts of the respiratory system in children and their interdependence in pathological processes in the respiratory system. The reliable existence of a risk ratio in the analysis of clinical and paraclinical indicators in pneumonia in children was established. Thus, clinical and pathogenetic features of the course of pneumonia in children at the present stage have been identified, which is clinically reflected in a low-productive cough in 91.7% of cases, shortness of breath in 86% of patients, with a predominance of the expiratory component and a predominant lesion of the lower parts of the right lung. A reliable relationship between clinical and paraclinical indicators and the risk ratio for pneumonia in children is noted.

source_records.abstract: Pneumonia is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in children under 5 years of age worldwide. Although most pneumonia-related deaths in children occur in developing countries, the burden of the disease is significant and there are significant health care costs associated with pneumonia in developed countries. The number of pneumonia deaths worldwide was estimated to be 0.76 million, while the all-cause mortality rate was 5.5 per 1000 live births in 2015. Although pneumonia incidence and mortality rates have declined significantly, hospital admissions and hospitalizations are increasing in both developing and developed countries. In recent large epidemiological studies in the United States (US), the annual incidence of communityacquired pneumonia (CAP) requiring hospitalization was 15.7 cases per 10,000 children, with the highest rate among children under 2 years of age, and similar trends are observed in Asian countries. As a result of these comprehensive etiological examinations in children, pathogens were identified in 81% of cases, viruses in 73%, pyogenic bacteria in 7%, and atypical bacteria such as M. The most frequently identified viruses were respiratory syncytial virus and parainfluenza virus, although adenovirus and human rhinovirus were the second most frequently identified viruses in a specific cohort of these studies. Given such a wide variety of etiological factors with the predominance of viral agents, especially in children under 5 years of age, it is possible to consider the presence of a type-specific clinical picture - pneumonic status with a layering of obstructive and catarrhal manifestations that are so characteristic of children of early and younger age. Objective: To establish clinical and pathogenetic relationships in the course of pneumonia in young children. Materials and methods. The medical histories of 36 children under 5 years of age who were being treated in the pulmonary monological department of the Uzhhorod City Clinical Children’s Hospital were processed. Children were admitted to the department for treatment on the 3rd - 5th day of the disease. The average age of the patients was 3.8±0.7 years. The examined group of children consisted of 19 boys and 17 girls. Clinical parameters (palpation, percussion, auscultation data) and paraclinical data - radiographic changes detected in pneumonia in children were recorded. Data were analyzed for statistical significance and search for their relationships (using SPPS21 (IBM Statistics.New York. USA)), descriptive statistics, Pearson Chi-Square analysis, relative risk (risk ratio) were used. Low-productive cough was observed in 92% of cases and bothered patients throughout the day. Dyspnea was not observed in 5 (14%) children, and in 17 (47%) cases, expiratory dyspnea was noted, mixed in 14 (39%). Manifestations of catarrhal syndrome - difficulty in nasal breathing, mucous discharge were observed in 25 (69%) patients. By localization of pneumonia, lower-lobe pneumonia was mainly found in 27 (75%) cases, upper-lobe pneumonia in 7 (19%) children and combined upper-lobe and lower-lobe pneumonia in 2 (6%) patients. The results of physical methods of research revealed that percussion dullness of percussion sound was observed in 18 (50%) cases, tympanitis in 15 (42%) patients, auscultatively children with manifestations of hard breathing prevailed in 32 (88.9%), locally weakened vesicular was heard in 14 (38.9%) cases. Auscultatively dry rales of various caliber were heard in 27 (75%) children, wet rales - in 9 (25%) patients, the phenomenon of crepitation was heard only in 21 (58.3%) cases. The X-ray picture of pneumonia in children was confirmed by the presence of foci of shadowing in all children and was accompanied in 21 (58.3) patients by an increase in the bronchopulmonary pattern on the X-ray. Analysis of clinical and paraclinical indicators revealed a high degree of reliable relationships between the pulmonary picture on the X-ray and difficult nasal breathing (p = 0.009), between the localization of the focus of pneumonia in the lower lobes of the lungs and the presence of hard breathing (p = 0.008). A somewhat lower degree of reliability was observed between the pulmonary picture on the X-ray and the phenomena of shortness of breath (p = 0.022) and between difficult nasal breathing and crepitus (p = 0.030). The revealed patterns indicate a close pathogenetic relationship between the upper and lower parts of the respiratory system in children and their interdependence in pathological processes in the respiratory system. The reliable existence of a risk ratio in the analysis of clinical and paraclinical indicators in pneumonia in children was established. Thus, clinical and pathogenetic features of the course of pneumonia in children at the present stage have been identified, which is clinically reflected in a low-productive cough in 91.7% of cases, shortness of breath in 86% of patients, with a predominance of the expiratory component and a predominant lesion of the lower parts of the right lung. A reliable relationship between clinical and paraclinical indicators and the risk ratio for pneumonia in children is noted.

title: Epidemiology, Clinical Characteristics, and Severity of Human Parainfluenza Virus Infection in Children from 2015-2025: A Scoping Review Protocol
abstract: The objective of this scoping review is to identify and map the available evidence on the epidemiology, clinical characteristics, and severity of HPIV infection in hospitalised children, and to identify comparisons within HPIV serotypes, with other respiratory viruses and risk factors for severe outcomes. Expected outcomes: - Evidence on the epidemiology, clinical characteristics, and severity of human parainfluenza virus (HPIV) infection in hospitalised children from 2015-2025 - The differences between HPIV serotypes (HPIV 1-4) in terms of epidemiology and clinical presentation - Comparison with other common respiratory viruses (e.g., RSV, influenza, human metapneumovirus) in terms of epidemiology and clinical severity - Risk factors associated with severe outcomes/re-admission of HPIV infection in children

title: Dynamic regulation-based stabilizing mutations are highly effective for designing RSV pre-fusion F mRNA vaccines
abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of respiratory tract infections and poses a serious threat to young children, older adults, and immunocompromised individuals. We previously designed a pre-fusion stabilized F protein (pre-F), TriM-5, using a dynamic regulation mechanism, and produced a recombinant protein-based vaccine candidate that exhibited potent protection against RSV. However, several studies have revealed that the stabilization of pre-F achieved in protein form may not be sufficient for application in mRNA vaccine development. Here, based on TriM-5, we designed an mRNA vaccine candidate to assess whether the dynamic regulation-based stabilizing mutations of TriM-5 are also effective in an mRNA format. The TriM-5 mRNA was codon-optimized using in-house software named NVSI_GAmRNAopt, which employed a genetic algorithm incorporating multiple empirical parameters for coding sequence (CDS) optimization, and encapsulated using lipid nanoparticles (LNPs). Mouse immunization showed that after CDS optimization, the IgG antibody titers increased approximately threefold, indicating the effectiveness of our codon-optimization algorithm. Compared with the Moderna RSV mRNA sequence encapsulated with our proprietary BM028 LNPs, the TriM-5 mRNA-LNP induced 3.03-fold higher neutralizing antibody titers against RSV A2 virus, along with significantly higher IFN-γ, IL-5 and IL-17A secretion levels, indicating its superior immunogenicity. Virus challenge experiments demonstrated that both TriM-5 mRNA-LNP and Moderna mRNA-LNP reduced lung viral loads effectively, with no obvious lung pathology. The designed TriM-5 mRNA-LNP exhibits good immunogenicity and protective efficacy, and thereby may serve as a promising candidate for further vaccine development.

title: Physicians’ Attitudes and Early Uptake Tendencies Toward the Newly Introduced Adult RSV Vaccine in Türkiye: A Nationwide Survey Study
